name: pce
why: A PC emulator lets you boot old machines and watch real firmware and DOS run inside a simulated box.

brief.what_it_is: PCE is a collection of microcomputer emulators, written in ANSI C. The homepage lists PCE/atarist (Atari ST and Mega ST models), PCE/ibmpc (IBM PC 5150 or PC/XT 5160), PCE/macplus (several classic Macintosh models), and PCE/rc759 (Regnecentralen RC759 Piccoline). The pages do not describe the inputs or outputs in detail. The brew executables also include pbit, pce-img, pce-sim405, pce-sim6502, pce-simarm, pce-sims32 and pfdc, which the fetched pages do not describe.
brief.why_it_exists: The pages give no stated motivation. The About text only says what the emulators cover.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages say nothing about installation, runtimes, or first-run setup. A Download section exists on the homepage but I did not follow it. Nothing beyond brew install was checked.
brief.standout: One project bundles several different historical machines (Atari ST, IBM PC, classic Mac, RC759) under one codebase rather than a single-machine emulator. The brew package also ships a set of simulator and disk tools alongside the machine emulators.
brief.status: Quiet. The newest release on the homepage news is PCE 20171220-3d8a53e, dated 2017-12-20. The homepage was last modified 2017-12-21. The About page was last modified 2013-08-20 and still says the project contains three emulators, which predates the RC759 and later entries. No newer news appeared on the pages I read.
brief.caveats: The About page is dated 2013 and its emulator count is out of date. The homepage news has no entries after December 2017. The brew caveats field is empty. I did not check build requirements, platform support, or the license terms beyond the About page's statement that it is GPL v2. The scout note's claim about watching DOS run is not stated on either page I read.
quotes: PCE is a collection of microcomputer emulators.
